alignment.benchmark: full-trajectory Umeyama Sim(3) on camera centres (evaluation only)
alignment.common_intersection: each condition re-aligned (own Sim(3)) on the frames ESTIMATED+associated in all of A, B, C
alignment.early_reference: first 20 % by time; OBSERVABLE iff n >= 10, GT RMS spread sv1 >= 0.05 m and scale > 0: rotation from orientations (chordal), scale/translation from positions; otherwise ROTATION_ONLY with scale/translation UNOBSERVABLE; never repaired with later GT
alignment.statement: no alignment is estimation or localisation; ATE after Sim(3) is not metric scale; GT world origin not recovered
alignment.w140_position_only_early: computed for continuity, never interpreted as drift

area_control.construction:
Deterministic static-region control with the same pixel area as exclusion mask H, disjoint from H.

    1. For each declared offset (fractions of W, H; wrap-around shift), shift H; pick the offset with the least overlap with
       H (ties -> first declared).  2. C = shifted \ H.  3. If |C| < |H|, grow C by adding non-H pixels in order of their
       distance to C (ties in raster order) until |C| = |H| or the background is exhausted (shortfall reported).
    Uses only the (RGB-derived) mask; never GT.
area_control.limitation: pixel-area matched, not feature-count matched; the removed-keypoint counts of B and C are reported

conventions:
W140 (EXPERIMENTAL, opt-in, scratch only): static-scene camera pose reconstruction -- pure numpy contracts and evaluation.

Isolated experimental camera-pose interface; NOT integrated into Production FramePose, MotionGraph, the S1 camera
calibration or any Blender root/spine/bone transform.

CONVENTIONS (frozen; never changed to improve a metric)
  * Camera optical frame "C" (OpenCV): +X right, +Y down, +Z forward (viewing direction).
  * T_WC(t) = [R_WC | c] maps camera-optical coordinates to world: X_W = R_WC X_C + c.  c is the CAMERA CENTER.
  * T_CW = T_WC^-1 = [R_CW | t_CW] with R_CW = R_WC^T, t_CW = -R_WC^T c (the "extrinsic translation" -- NOT the center).
  * Projection (OpenCV pixel convention: integer pixel coordinates are pixel CENTERS):
        x_C = R_CW X_W + t_CW;  u = fx x/z + cx,  v = fy y/z + cy.
    COLMAP uses a pixel-CORNER origin, so cx_colmap = cx_opencv + 0.5, cy_colmap = cy_opencv + 0.5.
  * Quaternions are stored SCALAR-LAST [qx, qy, qz, qw] (TUM order), unit norm, as rotation R_WC.
  * TUM groundtruth.txt "timestamp tx ty tz qx qy qz qw" = optical-center position and orientation of the RGB camera in
    the motion-capture world frame, i.e. exactly T_WC in the TUM world (metres).
  * Blender camera local axes: +X right, +Y up, -Z viewing.  R_WC(optical) = R_W,blendercam @ diag(1, -1, -1).
  * Monocular estimates live in an ARBITRARY world gauge with ARBITRARY scale ("scale_status": SCALE_AMBIGUOUS).  Any
    comparison to GT uses an evaluation-only Sim(3) alignment that never feeds back into estimation.

Frame status categories: ESTIMATED, PREDICTED_INTERPOLATED, LOST, UNOBSERVABLE, INVALID.

W141 (EXPERIMENTAL, opt-in, scratch only): dynamic-scene camera pose robustness -- masks, feature accounting, evaluation.

Isolated experimental extension of W140 (``app.experimental_camera_pose``, imported and reused UNCHANGED: conventions,
SE(3)/quaternion maths, GT association, Umeyama Sim(3), ATE/RPE, stationary baseline).  NOT integrated into Production,
FramePose, MotionGraph, the S1 camera calibration, root motion or the Dual-Stage Generator.

Conventions are W140's (T_WC optical OpenCV axes, scalar-last quaternions, SCALE_AMBIGUOUS monocular estimates, evaluation-
only alignment).  Additional W141 conventions:
  * Exclusion mask E (uint8, 255 = exclude from camera geometry) in image pixel coordinates (row = y, col = x).
  * COLMAP keep mask = 255 - E  (COLMAP drops keypoints on zero pixels).  COLMAP keypoint (x, y) uses a pixel-CORNER origin,
    so the pixel containing it is (floor(y), floor(x)); OpenCV centre coordinates are (x - 0.5, y - 0.5).
  * Condition B mask  = disk-dilate(RGB person mask, DILATE_PX).
  * Condition C mask  = area-matched static-region control built deterministically from B's mask (``area_control_mask``).
  * Condition D mask  = disk-dilate(oracle foreground mask, DILATE_PX)  (synthetic only, ORACLE diagnostic).

walking_static.authentication: official TUM HTTPS URL; byte size equals the server Content-Length; TUM publishes no checksum, so the downloaded SHA-256 is recorded as the identity

walking_xyz.authentication: official TUM HTTPS URL; byte size equals the server Content-Length; TUM publishes no checksum, so the downloaded SHA-256 is recorded as the identity

estimator.config: SIFT max 8192; sequential pairing overlap 10 quadratic, no loop detection; single PINHOLE camera with the given intrinsics, NOT refined; mapper defaults; random_seed 0; 8 threads; multiple models allowed; primary = largest
estimator.determinism: seeded, but multi-threaded mapping not bit-reproducible; exactly one official run per declared run
estimator.feature_exclusion: conditions B/C/D/oracle_areactrl run scripts/w141_colmap_masked_estimate.py, which executes the W140 estimator code unchanged with pycolmap.ImageReaderOptions().mask_path set to the condition's keep masks (COLMAP drops keypoints on zero pixels; images are never painted). Verified pre-declaration by the extraction-only check (0 keypoints on excluded pixels; masked set == unmasked set minus excluded).
inputs_only: RGB PNG frames (fr3: byte copies, already undistorted)
B/C: exclusion masks derived from the same RGB frames only
estimator.method: FROZEN W140 COLMAP incremental SfM (pycolmap 4.2.1, CPU), scripts/w140_colmap_estimate.py unchanged
never_inputs: oracle masks (except the labelled synthetic oracle diagnostics)

gates.classification: SUPPORTED: A or B passes the config gate on both real sequences; PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED: on one, or some configuration reaches the coverage floor and beats the baseline; NOT_YET_SUPPORTED otherwise; BLOCKED: a prerequisite fails. The masking-benefit verdict is reported separately. Never changed after results.
gates.config: per real sequence x condition: coverage >= 80% (denominator 300) AND Sim(3) ATE RMSE <= {'walking_static': 0.05, 'walking_xyz': 0.15} AND median rotation error <= 5.0 deg AND both ATE and median rotation below the stationary best-constant-pose baseline (added because walking_static's GT extent makes the ATE target non-discriminating)
gates.masking_benefit: B improves on A: (B coverage >= floor and A < floor) OR on the common intersection (n >= 30) ATE or median rotation lower by >= 20% and >= 0.005 m / 0.5 deg; AND B coverage >= A - 0.1; AND C distinct (C does not improve on A by the same rule, or B beats C by it). Verdicts DEMONSTRATED / NOT_ATTRIBUTABLE_TO_HUMAN_EXCLUSION / HARMFUL / UNNECESSARY (A passes) / NOT_DEMONSTRATED
gates.synthetic: clean run must reproduce W140's synthetic recovery/stationary gates; a condition is DISTURBED if ATE_rel > 2.0x clean and > clean + 0.2% of extent, or median rotation > clean + 0.5 deg, or coverage < clean - 0.1, or stationary-interval spurious motion fails the W140 thresholds; exclusion PREVENTS disturbance if the masked run is not DISTURBED while unmasked is

gt_association: W140 rule: linear position + SLERP between the bracketing GT samples, gap <= 0.05 s; evaluate stage only, after all estimate.json are frozen by SHA-256
metrics: GT-referenced spikes (consecutive relative error > max(5.0 x median, 0.02 m / 2.0 deg))
keypoints / retained / removed per frame from the COLMAP database
model observations inside RGB person masks (contamination proxy)
frames with < 200 retained keypoints (inadequate background evidence)
Spearman correlation of per-frame occupancy with A error and with A-B error difference
synthetic: per-segment errors, stationary-interval spurious motion, rotation-interval spurious translation, landmark distance to static boxes, oracle-mask contamination, RGB-vs-oracle mask IoU
pre_declaration_disclosures: dev check of COLMAP mask_path on two W140 synthetic frames (dev/masktest): 0 keypoints on excluded pixels, masked = unmasked minus excluded

dev prototype of the synthetic dynamic scene on 4 frames (dev/syn_proto) and of Mask R-CNN on them (person IoU 0.29-0.86 vs the oracle); afterwards the nearer occluder was moved closer to the camera (y -1.0 -> -1.6, start x -1.4 -> -0.9, speed 0.90 -> 0.85) to raise image occupancy; no estimator, matching or GT-scored output existed at that point; the occluders were not adjusted to improve detection

the first preflight run crashed in build_masks because Blender writes the oracle masks as 3-channel grey PNGs (MASK_CONTRACT refused a (480, 640, 3) array); read_mask now accepts a grey 3-channel image (refusing non-grey) and the preflight was re-run from scratch; the crashed run is kept at results/preflight_crash1_oracle_mask_channels (no estimator output, no GT involved)

the RGB masks and their occupancy statistics were computed in the preflight (no GT involved) before this declaration; DILATE_PX, thresholds and area-control offsets were fixed in the instrument code before the masks were generated

segmentation.selection_rationale: one bounded, widely used, licensed instance-segmentation checkpoint with a COCO person class, available through the existing torchvision install; no model search, no training
segmentation.settings: CPU float32, model's own resize, label person, score >= 0.5, soft mask >= 0.5, union over instances
